subject: Throughput sizing follow-up: Finex Payments (post-call)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Cho <alan.cho@finexpay.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-22T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: throughput/latency targets & next steps

Hi Alan — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + a few follow-ups so we can size Dedicated capacity for Finex: 

1) SLOs and latency targets: you mentioned 95th pct latency target of 250ms for single-turn requests and a 500ms target for streaming responses to first token. Confirm?
2) Typical request/response size: you said most requests are ~150 tokens prompt and 60 tokens response on average — please confirm avg prompt/response tokens and max tokens per request.
3) QPS vs concurrency: what are your expected steady-state QPS and peak QPS (e.g., 10 QPS steady, 100 QPS peak burst)? Also, how many concurrent sessions do you expect to keep KV caches warm?
4) Streaming: are you doing token-by-token streaming in prod for conversational flows, and do you need guaranteed first-token latency under 500ms?

I've attached a short template (finex_metrics_qps.csv) you can fill with hourly QPS / tokens-per-request distribution; that'll let Rafael produce a sizing estimate. Next steps: if you can reply with the CSV + any latency SLO clarifications by EOD Wednesday, Rafael will send a draft sizing and cost estimate by Friday.

--
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
[attachment: finex_metrics_qps.csv (CSV, 12KB)]

From: Alan Cho <alan.cho@finexpay.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyanka Mehta <priyanka@finexpay.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T16:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: throughput/latency targets & next steps

Thanks Neha — great summary. Quick answers inline: 

1) Latency: 95p target 200-250ms for non-streaming inference; for streaming we need first-token under 400-500ms depending on region.
2) Tokens: avg prompt 140-170 tokens, avg response 50-80 tokens; max combined tokens we send occasionally up to ~1024 for long-document summarization flows.
3) Traffic: steady-state 8-12 QPS (US region), peak bursts up to ~120 QPS during promo windows. Concurrency: we expect ~20 long-lived conversational sessions that benefit from warm KV cache, but most sessions are short-lived.
4) Yes, we stream responses for chat UI in prod for low-latency UX. First-token requirement is important for US customers.

I'll attach an hourly QPS export for last 30 days — see finex_metrics_qps.csv. Let me know if you need any more detail.

–Alan
Alan Cho
Head of Platform Engineering, Finex Payments
alan.cho@finexpay.com
[attachment: finex_metrics_qps.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Cho <alan.cho@finexpay.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-22T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: throughput/latency targets & next steps

Alan — thanks for the upload and clarifications, this is helpful. High-level sizing notes based on the CSV and the targets you listed: 

- Baseline: for 10 QPS steady with avg token sizes (~210 tokens total per request), we estimate needing a pool equivalent to ~4 x A100-class GPUs under our optimized runtime to meet 95p 250ms non-streaming SLO with headroom for autoscale. 
- Bursts: for the 120 QPS promotional peaks, we recommend a combination of burst capacity + model-routing to a slightly higher-latency quantized variant to absorb short spikes without impacting cost. That equates to ~8-10 GPUs for <5 minute peaks if fully served on the same model flavor.
- Streaming: to guarantee first-token under 500ms, use a warm concurrency of ~16 sessions pinned on hot workers (KV cache warm). We can reserve a small pool for pinned streaming lanes.
- Long documents (1024 tokens): plan for higher token processing time and memory; those should be routed to larger-instance workers and/or use chunked-processing patterns we outlined in the notes.

I attached a short PDF with the sizing assumptions and a table mapping QPS/token combos to GPU counts and estimated cost (redwood_sizing_notes.pdf). Next steps: if Finex is comfortable, we can propose a Dedicated trial with a reserved baseline pool plus burst capacity for 30 days to validate real-world latencies and cost. If you want, we can schedule a 30 min sync tomorrow to walk through the sizing table and rollout options.

Cheers,
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
[attachment: redwood_sizing_notes.pdf (PDF, 220KB)]
